findings.where: artifacts/gn1/a2/evidence.py:157 (recognised forge outcomes), evidence.py:295 and run_gpu_line.py:57 (not-admitted predicate); installed forge-gpu-run:281,285
findings.defect: The installed forge-gpu-run has a third lease refusal, outcome 'rechecked-out' with exit 75 (the window changed while it waited for the lock, or the budget fell below --min after the wait). A2 recognises only ran/timeout/window-closed/no-window/no-lock, so it maps that log row to 'unrecognized', records the attempt as admitted and failed, and the parent then refuses every retry of the label ('label already has an admitted attempt'). This is R1-F08's exact consequence: every line must rerun in a new run root. D7 requires a 75/76 lease refusal to be 'not admitted' and retryable.
findings.reproduction: rev2/hostile_rev2.py part b, case B1, with the REAL forge-gpu-run (summary, window file and lock redirected under /tmp/gn1_rev2_forge; CPU sleeper child). REV2 holds the scratch lock, appends a COOLDOWN event while the runner waits, then releases it. Forge log row: rechecked-out 75. Parent receipt: admission admitted, forge_outcome unrecognized, passed false. The retry exits 1 with 'AssertionError: label already has an admitted attempt'. The scorer fails baseline_focus with its single admitted attempt. Receipt: rev2/hostile_rev2_b.json.
findings.fix: Add 'rechecked-out' to forge_outcome's recognised set. Treat (rc 75, cause no-window or rechecked-out) and (rc 76, cause no-lock), with no child_result.json, as not admitted in both run_gpu_line.py and recompute_line. Add a G4 control that uses each outcome word the installed runner can log, read from the runner rather than from a stand-in.

findings.where: tensor_cuda/tests/test_groupnorm_gn1.py:139-142; artifacts/gn1/a2/hostile_forge.py:76-79; G4_CONTROLS.md rows Generic_RuntimeError_not_kill and Unregistered_TypeError_not_kill
findings.defect: D2 counts a kill only for an AssertionError, or a ValueError/TypeError refusal from GroupNorm. The sealed test re-raises ANY RuntimeError, ValueError or TypeError from layer(x) in _check_values as AssertionError, so a generic, non-device engine RuntimeError is counted as a kill. G4's two controls claim the opposite, but they inject exception_class RuntimeError/TypeError directly into a stand-in summary, a shape the sealed test file cannot produce for these calls. The controls are vacuous against the real pipeline, and A2's report does not disclose the widening. The protection against environmental false kills then rests only on the device-pattern list (which the REV2 engine census found complete for the GroupNorm path) and on the candidate-focus precondition.
findings.reproduction: rev2/q3_probe.py case P1: the real test ID test_forward_values[float32-r3-n2-g2-default], the real candidate nn.py and A2's real Reports plugin, under A2's NumPy engine stand-in whose pow raises RuntimeError('pow: unsupported exponent path'). Plugin: exception_class AssertionError. evidence.acceptable_killers counts it as a kill, and the device veto does not fire. Receipt: rev2/q3_probe.json.
findings.fix: This is a lead decision. Either (a) amend D2 to state that a registered valid input refused by GroupNorm or by any engine op it calls is a kill unless it carries a device pattern, and replace the two controls with controls that run the real test file (as P1 does); or (b) narrow the wrapper to the registered engine refusal texts (for example 'reshape: element count mismatch', 'ew_binary dtype mismatch', 'shapes not broadcastable') and let every other exception propagate with its own class.

findings.where: artifacts/gn1/a2/run_gpu_tests.py:37-39; evidence.py:170-177 (comment: 'must originate in the GroupNorm frame'); G4 control Registered_refusal_positive ('GroupNorm-origin')
findings.defect: groupnorm_refusal is true when ANY traceback entry is GroupNorm.forward or GroupNorm.__init__ in nn.py. It does not check where the exception was raised. A ValueError or TypeError raised by an engine call made from inside GroupNorm is therefore classed as a registered GroupNorm refusal.
findings.reproduction: rev2/q3_probe.py case P2: test_constructor_defaults, with the engine's tensor factory raising TypeError while GroupNorm.__init__ allocates its parameters. The plugin records exception_class TypeError with groupnorm_refusal true, and acceptable_killers counts it as a kill. Receipt: rev2/q3_probe.json.
findings.fix: Classify by the innermost entry (excinfo.traceback[-1]): it must be GroupNorm.forward or __init__ in the arm's nn.py, ideally on one of the registered raise lines. Add a control with a callee-raised TypeError under GroupNorm.

findings.where: artifacts/gn1/a2/run_gpu_line.py:83 (outer_timeout_exit=rc in (124, 137)); the field is not checked by the scorer (evidence.py:317)
findings.defect: The receipt keeps A1's flag under a new name, and it is still true for every 124. With the real runner it is true when forge's own deadline fired, when the window closed, and when the child's inner timeout fired: three cases where the outer bound did not fire. In the one case where the outer bound did fire, the cause is recorded only as 'log-exit-mismatch', because forge logged 'ran 143' after the TERM. A receipt can therefore still state an outer timeout that did not happen.
findings.reproduction: rev2/hostile_rev2.py part b with the REAL forge-gpu-run. B2: forge 'timeout 124', outer_timeout_exit true. B3: 'window-closed 124', true. B5: 'ran 124' (inner child timeout), true. B4 (outer bound fired): forge 'ran 143', forge_outcome 'log-exit-mismatch'. Receipt: rev2/hostile_rev2_b.json.
findings.fix: Derive the outer timeout from the runner's row. It fired iff rc is 124 or 137 and the row is missing, or the row says 'ran' with a logged exit of 143 or 137 that differs from rc. Record it as cause 'outer-timeout', drop or rename the old flag, and have the scorer recompute it.

findings.defect: The D5 check `not isinstance(v, int)` refuses NumPy integer counts: np.int64, np.int32 and np.uint8 with the value 2 or 6. These are positive integers, so they are inside D5's domain ('not a positive integer (bool excluded)'). A1 accepted them, and PyTorch 2.11 accepts them in both the constructor and forward. GroupNorm now refuses inputs it should accept. No test pins either behaviour.
findings.reproduction: rev2/d5_probe.py, constructor rows num_groups/np_int64, np_int32, np_uint8 and num_channels/np_int64, np_int32, np_uint8. A1: accepted. A2: ValueError 'must be a positive integer (bool excluded)'. torch: accepted. Receipt: rev2/d5_probe.json.
findings.fix: Accept any integral value through operator.index, excluding bool and numpy.bool_, and store int(value). Add accept tests for NumPy integers and a refusal test for numpy.bool_.

findings.closes_or_relates: same class as R1-F06; not listed in D5
findings.defect: Parameter shape is not validated. A weight with C elements in a non-vector shape, (2,3), (6,1) or (1,6,1), is silently reshaped to [1,C,...] and used. A weight of the wrong size is refused only by an incidental engine reshape RuntimeError (kernels.cu:759), the same incidental-refusal pattern R1-F06 reported for a channel mismatch. PyTorch refuses all three shapes ('Expected weight to be a vector of size equal to the number of channels in input'). D5 did not list parameter shape, so this is a scope gap in the order rather than a deviation by A2.
findings.reproduction: rev2/d5_probe.py, param_shape rows: A2 accepted, torch refused (RuntimeError). Receipt: rev2/d5_probe.json.
findings.fix: In forward, refuse with ValueError when weight.ndim != 1, bias.ndim != 1, or either shape[0] != C. Add a test and a mutant for each check.

findings.defect: If the parent dies after creating attempt-NNNN but before writing parent_result.json (an interrupt, the staged outer `timeout 350s`, a session loss), every later parent for that label crashes reading the missing receipt, and the scorer fails the line. The label cannot be rerun in that root, so every line must rerun in a new root. The outcome is fail-closed: no false pass.
findings.reproduction: rev2/hostile_rev2.py part c, case C7. The parent is SIGKILLed after its child wrote child_result.json. The retry exits 1 with FileNotFoundError on attempt-0001/parent_result.json. The scorer shows the line failed. Receipt: rev2/hostile_rev2_c.json.
findings.fix: Treat an attempt without a parent receipt as incomplete. If its child_result.json exists, the next parent finalises (evaluates) that attempt rather than retrying, to prevent retry-until-pass. If the child never started, record the attempt as not admitted and allow a retry. The scorer lists incomplete attempts.

findings.defect: M14 edits the default argument on the `def __init__` line (nn.py:511). That line executes when the class is defined, at import, not when the witness runs. A2's trace counts import-time lines (its executed_lines start at line 1), so '[511] -> [511]' would hold for any test. The kill itself is real: the witness asserts layer.eps == 1e-5 and fails on the mutant. But the reach claim does not come from the witness.
findings.reproduction: rev2/q5_mutant_trace.py traces only the witness's call phase. Line 511 is not executed there for M14; every other mutant's edit line is. The M14 witness exits 1 on the mutant and 0 on the candidate. Receipt: rev2/q5_mutant_trace.json.
findings.fix: Restrict traces to the call phase. Record M14's reach as default-argument binding observed by the witness's call path.
